description: This solution decodes left vs right 2-second finger-tapping fNIRS optical-density trials by flattening the (136,8) trial arrays to vectors, then z-scales (standardizes) each channel/bin using only the training set. Feature selection is performed via univariate ANOVA F-score on the training trials, keeping the top 120 features (empirically safe for ~400 trials, high-dimensional data). A Linear Support Vector Machine with L2 penalty, balanced class weights, and a deterministic seed is fit to train_x and train_y. This fast and robust approach suits high-dimensional, moderate-sample-size fNIRS data and avoids overfitting. The trained pipeline is then used to predict test_x; test trials are standardized (and selected) with metrics from the training set only. Each trial is predicted independently, one label per test trial. No information about test_y is used for model selection, fitting, or transforms. The code is suitable for held-out subject/session generalization.
